summary: Fewer people are cleared to sit China's civil service exam for the first time in seven years, but about 97 still compete for each job as young graduates seek security.
body: Nearly 3.94 million people signed up this month for China's national civil service exam, which fills jobs in central government bodies [^1][^2]. After screening, about 3.45 million were approved to sit it, the first fall in seven years, down 7.2% from 3.72 million last year [^1]. Caixin says the drop seems to come from tighter checks, including new identity verification against fraudulent sign-ups, not weaker interest [^1][^2]. The government plans to hire about 35,700 people, roughly 2,400 fewer than last year, so there are about 97 approved candidates for every opening, and far more for some county-level posts [^1][^2].

Why young people line up: a government post is known as an "iron rice bowl" because it is seen as secure for life. China expects a record 12.7 million university graduates this year, and the unemployment rate for urban 16- to 24-year-olds not in school was about 18% in September [^2]. Some graduates have turned to food delivery, freelance or factory work as entry-level openings shrink, with weak consumer demand, a long property slump and worries about AI replacing jobs all in the background [^2]. Since last year the age limit for the exam has been raised from 35 to 38 [^2]. My read: when the most sought-after job in a country is the safest one, that says a lot about how young people see the private economy. It was otherwise a quieter day for China tech news.

reads.title: China Civil Service Exam Draws 4 Million Applicants for 35,000 Jobs
reads.summary: The numbers behind China's civil service exam rush, and how youth unemployment and a tight job market push graduates toward government work.
